items.title: Frank Strazzeri interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: So I grew up as a little kid listening to him play.

ctx.x: Can you recall any of the tunes he played that might have stuck in your ear?

Oh he used to play “Avalon” and “After You’ve Gone,” and “Indiana,” and “Idaho.” Well you know, of course everybody’s forever playing “Body and Soul” and “How High the Moon” and those kind of things. They used to play things out of Benny Goodman, kind of thing. Whatever we heard of Benny Goodman, he was a disciple of that era. So I grew up as a little kid listening to him play. He used to play in the house. He was a good solo piano player. He played real good by himself. © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
Did you ever get to go out and hear him in a jazz environment?
